sections.title: Atlas: camera control in image or video

items.label: Hook: the third chapter
items.copy:
Agents that don't stop when you close your laptop, you can now run jobs for hours or days, or be 'always on,' unlocking a plethora of new ways to leverage AI.

It's gone from prompting, to agentic, now persistence.

To summarize, Grok is furthest ahead on letting one agent run indefinitely without you. OpenAI's got the most ambitious version, they just haven't shipped it. Anthropic has shipped pieces one at a time, they haven't done a good job marketing persistence.

Full issue: [link]

items.label: Forever timelines
items.copy: Regardless, start playing with what you can do by running agents across 'forever' timelines, it changes the way you think about use.

items.label: Better at finishing
items.copy: Plainly: it is not significantly smarter, but it is much better at finishing. Gains are on working for hours and recovering from mistakes.

items.label: 3-post thread: two reviewers
items.copy:
1/ Before execution, I currently run 2x second opinions, all from Claude code, which runs Codex and GrokBuild straight through the terminal.

2/ Before I execute on any build they beat up the plan and improve it.

3/ If you run two reviewers, move the first one's write-up out of the folder before you start the second. Mine read the other's report and started agreeing with it.

items.label: Scope, then the last mile
items.copy: Scope with 5.1, hand the plan to something cheap, then bring 5.1 back for the final pass. The last mile is where the recovery behaviour earns its price.

items.label: Twenty-four frames
items.copy: Feed it a handful of ground-level shots and it rebuilds the space in 3D, including angles not captured. Twenty-four frames of phone video, about a second of walking, is enough to build an environment.

items.label: Hook: two to three times faster
items.copy:
The average adult types 52 words a minute at a desk, 36 on a phone.

Dictation studies clock people between 90 and 160 words a minute, two to three times faster (Testing caveat, most of those measures are people reading prepared text aloud on a phone).

It is not for writing. Spoken sentences are longer, looser and more repetitive than written ones, good writing requires sitting and thinking, but ideation and capturing thoughts is where transcription excels.

Apple's dictation is already on your Mac, it costs nothing, and it is good enough to find out whether you like working this way.

Full issue: [link]

items.label: 3-post thread: Whisper vs Wispr
items.copy:
1/ Whisper is a speech-recognition model OpenAI released for free in 2022. It is not an app. Anyone can run it on their own machine.

2/ Wispr Flow is a paid app from a different company. It runs in the cloud.

3/ MacWhisper is a paid Mac app that runs Whisper locally on your own machine.

items.label: Hook: build the templates first
items.copy:
I started by building the things I needed, social assets and layouts, and it was so iterative on the smallest details that it was slower than doing it myself. The fix is to build the templates first.

Point Claude at your best previous work alongside your references and have it build templates from both, iterating for variety.

Every INTAKE issue now turns into social assets for LinkedIn, stories and Pinterest, three sets of dimensions, in minutes. Work that used to take me a few hours.

Full issue: [link]

items.label: Outline first
items.copy:
Big files break the pipe.

Ask for the outline first, then pull only the frames you need.

items.label: Decks become cleanup
items.copy: Use it for decks. Slides is writable now, decks are a huge waste of time that now become a cleanup pass.
